chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Circumcise your children on the seventh day, for it is purer, more pleasant, and causes the flesh to grow faster. Indeed, the earth becomes impure from the urine of the uncircumcised for forty mornings.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time for circumcising children in Shia Islam and what is the reasoning?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith linking the Sunnah of circumcision on the seventh day to both physical hygiene and ritual purity (taharah). The narration highlights a specific jurisprudential nuance: the urine of the 'aghlaf' (uncircumcised) is considered so potent in defiling the earth that it remains impure for forty days, underscoring the importance of removing the foreskin to maintain ritual cleanliness in daily worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-6 (The compiler of the book narrated) that my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Muslim al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Circumcise your child on the seventh day after his birth. That is much better and it would heal faster. In fact, the Earth becomes filthy for forty days due to the urination of one who is not circumcised.”
